claim: The Agent Skills standard defines six frontmatter fields: name and description are required; license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools are optional.

value.metadata: map of string keys to string values

notes: The name may not start or end with a hyphen or contain two in a row, which the pattern encodes.

claim: The standard recommends keeping SKILL.md under 500 lines and its instructions under about 5,000 tokens, with file references one level deep from SKILL.md, written as relative paths.

Claude Code reads twenty skill frontmatter fields, all optional: the standard's six plus when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths and shell.
notes: The listing shows description and when_to_use together, cut at 1,536 characters. There is no field named auto-activate.

claim: Claude Code ignores a frontmatter field it does not know, without an error, so a misspelled or invented field silently does nothing.
notes: This is why check reports fields that no tool reads: nothing else will.

claim: Claude Code replaces $ARGUMENTS (all arguments), $ARGUMENTS[N] and $N (one argument, from 0), named $arguments, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} and ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} in a skill, and runs !`command` blocks before the skill reaches the model.
notes: $0 is the first argument only, not every argument. None of these are part of the Agent Skills standard, so a portable skill gives a plain-words fallback.

claim: Codex requires name and description in SKILL.md and documents no other frontmatter fields. UI details and implicit invocation live in an optional agents/openai.yaml next to it.
notes: With allow_implicit_invocation false, Codex never picks the skill from a prompt, but $skill-name still runs it.

claim: Codex spends at most 2% of the model's context window on its list of skills by default and shortens descriptions first; on a Mac with more than 160 skills installed, Codex 0.159.3 removed every description and left 164 skills out of the list.

sources.title: Our test: codex exec on a Mac with many skills installed

notes: The warning Codex printed: 'Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 164 additional skills were not included in the model-visible skills list.' This is why tokens reports the listing cost of every skill.

claim: Cursor reads name and description (required), disable-model-invocation, paths, icon, color and metadata, and the older globs as a fallback.
notes: Not confirmed on a real Cursor install: its CLI is not on the test Mac.

claim: Antigravity requires name and description in SKILL.md, and reads a plugin's skills from skills/<name>/SKILL.md.

sources.title: Antigravity: skills (the same text ships inside the app as agy-customizations/docs/skills.md, app 2.3.1)

notes: No field for running a skill only when asked.

claim: Claude Code 2.1.299, Codex 0.159.3 and the Antigravity CLI 1.4.2 each still load a skill whose frontmatter carries fields they do not use (when_to_use, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation, an invented auto-activate, metadata).

sources.title: Our test: two skills, one plain and one with extra fields, listed headless by each tool

notes: Each tool was asked to list its skills in a folder holding both. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 could not run: Google closed it to free personal accounts (reason UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT). So a tool-specific field such as disable-model-invocation is safe to ship in a shared SKILL.md.

claim: Each tool reads project skills from its own folder: Claude Code from .claude/skills; Codex, Antigravity and Cursor from .agents/skills; Gemini CLI from .gemini/skills or .agents/skills. Cursor also reads Claude Code's and Codex's folders.
notes: Antigravity's .agents/skills was confirmed by the field test above, where it listed skills from that folder.

claim: Gemini CLI 0.62.0 refuses to run for a free personal Google account and points to Antigravity instead.

sources.title: Our test: gemini -p on a personal account

notes: Paid and API-key accounts still run it. bench skips Gemini CLI without a key and says why.

claim: Claude Code 2.1.299, Codex 0.159.3 and the Antigravity CLI 1.4.2 each still load a skill whose description holds an unquoted ": " (for example "Use when: ..."), which a strict YAML reader rejects as a second key.

sources.title: Our test: one skill with the colon quoted and one without, listed headless by each tool

notes: So check reports it as a warning, not an error: the skill loads where tested, and quoting the value makes it safe in every YAML reader. 37 of 1,295 skills on the test Mac had it.

claim: Claude Code fits the list of skill names and descriptions into a budget of 1% of the model's context window; when the list overflows it keeps every name but drops descriptions, starting with the skills invoked least.

sources.title: Claude Code: skills, 'Skill descriptions are cut short'

notes: On the test Mac (Opus 5.5, a 1,000,000-token window, 260 skills installed), /context put the Skills row at 9.9k tokens, which matches a budget of 1% counted in tokens, and showed many skills as name-only. A skill without its description in the list can't be matched to a request, so a plugin's listing cost decides whether its skills still trigger.
